requested_parts: What makes lands adjacent across boards
answers.answer: Lands are adjacent when they touch by border or corner, including across boards. Only lands touching printed Ocean are Coastal; other outer edges are cliffs. Ocean is not normally a land or in play. A land is not adjacent to itself, but is at Range 0 of itself and within any greater Range, including Range 1.

evidence.text: Each balanced board has eight lands, two each of Jungle, Mountain, Sands and Wetland. Lands are adjacent if they touch by border **or corner**, including across boards. Ocean is not normally a land or in play. Only lands touching a printed Ocean are Coastal; the other outside edges are cliffs, not coast. Other lands are Inland.

A land is not adjacent to itself, so cannot Gather/Push to itself. It is at Range 0 of itself and hence within any greater Range. An unrestricted “Move” can move a piece to its current land and counts as movement, unlike Gather/Push, which require adjacency.

evidence.text: **Growth:** Choose one boxed Growth option unless your panel specifies otherwise. Perform all its instructions if possible, in any order you choose. If an instruction is impossible, do as much as possible and skip that part; an explicit cost for an option must be paid in full to choose it. Common effects:

Each turn follows **Spirit Phase → Fast Power Phase → Invader Phase → Slow Power Phase → Time Passes**. Finish a phase before beginning the next. Players choose the order of Powers within the appropriate Power Phase, completing one before the next. All players act simultaneously within a phase and may discuss freely. Each Spirit must finish its own Growth → Gain Energy → Play/Pay in that order, but may wait to see another Spirit's Growth or draws before making choices. **Every Spirit must finish the entire Spirit Phase before any Fast Power resolves.**

evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. After **gaining a Major**, Forget one of your cards permanently. You may Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel, unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain. requested_parts: Slow card eligibility and innate eligibility
answers.answer: A Fast Gift of Strength/Powerstorm permission may wait until the Repeat is exercised, so a later-played card may qualify while in play. A Slow card may be Repeated and uses its current assigned speed; these permissions repeat Power Cards, not Innates. Repeat does not grant the card’s printed Elements again.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]

A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.
